overview: ASML Holding N.V. is a Dutch semiconductor equipment company and the world's sole supplier of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems, which are indispensable for manufacturing advanced chips at 7nm and below. Listed on both Nasdaq (ASML, USD) and Euronext Amsterdam (ASML.AS, EUR), the company reports financials in euros and holds a 100% monopoly in EUV lithography alongside dominant share in deep ultraviolet (DUV) systems. ASML's primary customers are TSMC, Samsung, and Intel, who collectively depend on ASML to manufacture chips powering the global AI infrastructure buildout.

business_model.summary: ASML generates revenue through two primary streams: net system sales (approximately 72% of FY2025 revenue at €24.5B) and Installed Base Management or IBM (approximately 28% at €8.2B), covering service contracts, upgrades, spare parts, and field options. The business features high barriers to entry, extreme customer lock-in through proprietary technology, and a growing recurring-revenue service base driven by an expanding installed machine fleet.

revenue_streams.name: EUV Systems
revenue_streams.description: Extreme ultraviolet lithography systems for advanced chip production at 7nm and below. Includes Low-NA EUV (NXE series, ~€200M ASP) and first commercial High-NA EUV shipments (EXE:5200B series, ~€380-400M ASP). ASML targeting at least 60 Low-NA EUV units in 2026.

revenue_streams.name: DUV Systems
revenue_streams.description: Deep ultraviolet lithography systems for mature and some advanced nodes. China accounted for ~33% of total FY2025 revenue but is expected to decline to ~20% in 2026 as export controls tighten. Proposed MATCH Act in the US threatens remaining DUV sales to China, worth ~5% of total revenue.

revenue_streams.name: Installed Base Management (IBM)
revenue_streams.description: High-margin recurring revenue from service contracts, upgrades, spare parts, and field options for the installed equipment base. IBM revenue grew from €6.5B (FY2024) to €8.2B (FY2025), a 26% increase. Management expects continued strong IBM growth in 2026 as the installed base expands.

business_model.customer_type: B2B - Major semiconductor manufacturers and foundries (TSMC, Samsung, Intel Foundry, SK Hynix, Micron, SMIC)
business_model.geographic_mix: China ~33% (FY2025, expected to fall to ~20% in FY2026); South Korea ~25%; Taiwan ~22%; Europe and Americas together ~20%

main_competitors: Nikon (DUV only, i-line and ArF systems)
xLight (US-funded startup targeting laser source technology, pre-commercial)
China state-backed EUV development (estimated 10-15 years behind commercial viability)
competitive_position.market_position: 100% monopoly in EUV lithography globally; dominant 80%+ share in advanced DUV immersion lithography; no credible commercial EUV competitor exists or is foreseeable within the decade

moat_factors.description: 30+ years and over $9 billion cumulative R&D to develop EUV technology that fires high-power lasers at molten tin droplets to generate 13.5nm extreme ultraviolet light. The physics, precision, and supply chain integration required are irreplicable. No competitor has achieved EUV commercialization.

ASML controls critical sub-systems including Zeiss SMT high-precision optics (25% equity stake) and Cymer laser sources (wholly owned subsidiary). These components are not available to would-be competitors and require decades of co-development.

Chip manufacturers have invested billions in ASML-compatible processes, fab infrastructure, process recipes, and workforce training. Migrating to an alternative technology would require retooling entire fabs, which is commercially and technically prohibitive.

Order backlog stood at €38.8 billion at end of FY2025, providing multi-year revenue visibility. Each EUV system has 12-18 month delivery lead times and contains ~100,000 components from 5,000+ suppliers, creating further barriers to capacity scale-up for any entrant.

ASML is already commercializing the next generation: High-NA EUV (EXE:5200 series), which has a 0.55 numerical aperture vs 0.33 for Low-NA and is required for sub-2nm node manufacturing. Intel installed the first production EXE:5200B, and SK hynix is ramping. This extends the technology lead by another decade.

Export controls on EUV and advanced DUV to China restrict competitor access to ASML's primary restricted markets, but also limit ASML's own China addressable market. The barriers protect ASML's installed base outside China from competitive substitution.

weaknesses: Heavy customer concentration: TSMC alone represents ~33% of revenue, top 3 customers likely exceed 70%
Geopolitical exposure: Dutch company at the center of US-China semiconductor technology war
China revenue dependency: China was 33% of FY2025 revenue, dropping to ~20% in FY2026 as export controls bite
Cyclicality: Revenue tied to semiconductor capex cycles that can swing 20-30% annually
Single-product category: All revenue tied to lithography equipment with no material diversification into etch, deposition, or process control

growth_drivers: AI infrastructure supercycle: Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Alphabet) committed over $300B in AI capex for 2025-2026 combined, driving sustained demand for leading-edge semiconductor capacity
TSMC capacity expansion: TSMC raised 2026 capex to $38-42B+ to meet AI chip demand, with major fab expansions in Taiwan, Arizona, Japan, and Germany — all requiring ASML EUV tools

High-NA EUV ramp: Production EXE:5200B systems now shipping commercially (Intel 14A node, SK hynix HBM); each unit priced at ~€380-400M vs ~€200M for Low-NA, providing significant ASP tailwind as mix shifts

Memory upgrade cycle: Advanced DRAM (including HBM for AI accelerators) requires EUV layers to achieve higher capacity and bandwidth; HBM demand from NVIDIA, AMD, and AI chip vendors driving memory capex
Installed Base Management growth: IBM grew 26% YoY in FY2025 to €8.2B; expanding installed fleet and service intensity will continue to grow this high-margin recurring stream
Low-NA EUV volume increase: ASML targeting at least 60 Low-NA EUV systems in FY2026 (up from 44 in FY2025) and potentially 80 in FY2027 if demand supports it
Technology intensity compounding: Each node shrink requires more EUV exposure layers per wafer, increasing tool demand per unit of wafer capacity independent of fab count growth
2030 market opportunity: Semiconductor equipment TAM expanding alongside continued AI-driven capacity investment; ASML targeting €44-60B revenue by 2030 from €32.7B in FY2025

business.description: TSMC represents approximately one-third of total revenue. Top 3 customers likely exceed 70% of sales. Any major capex reduction, fab delay, or demand shock at a key customer would materially impact ASML results.

Revenue is tied to industry capex cycles. While AI demand provides a stronger structural underpinning than prior cycles, historical downturns (e.g., 2023 when EUV revenue fell ~14% and total net sales dropped) confirm ASML is not immune. Post-2027 visibility beyond committed orders is limited.

business.risk: DUV loophole closure and China demand loss
business.description: China had been exploiting older DUV tools (multi-patterning techniques) to approach near-cutting-edge nodes. As export controls tighten, China revenue is falling from 33% to ~20% in 2026. Remaining China DUV revenue faces further risk from MATCH Act proposals.

financial.description: Early High-NA EUV systems carry higher manufacturing costs during ramp. Q3 2025 gross margin dipped to 51.6%, below the 52-53% range, partly reflecting product transition effects. Path to 56-60% long-term margins depends on High-NA mix and learning curve improvements.

ASML trades at a substantial premium to the broader market and semiconductor equipment peers. Any guidance miss, macro deterioration, or escalation of geopolitical risk could trigger significant multiple compression. Analyst consensus average price target is approximately €1,574 with a 'Strong Buy' rating from 35+ analysts.

regulatory.risk: MATCH Act - US DUV export ban proposal
regulatory.description: Bipartisan US legislation introduced in April 2026 (MATCH Act) would ban DUV lithography exports to China and require Dutch alignment with US standards within 150 days, with FDPR sanctions otherwise. Cleared House Foreign Affairs Committee in April 2026. Could eliminate ~5% of total ASML revenue if enacted in current form. Also threatens DUV service and maintenance revenues for already-installed China systems.

regulatory.risk: US allegations of EUV component diversion to China
regulatory.description: In June 2026, US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick accused ASML in private meetings of allowing EUV machine components to reach China in violation of export controls. ASML formally denied the claims, publishing documentation accounting for all 314 EUV systems worldwide (none in China). US authorities cited unspecified evidence of EUV-related shipments. If the US finds ASML in violation of export control obligations, it could result in restrictions on ASML's ability to export to any market using US-origin technology (FDPR), representing an existential regulatory risk.

Netherlands joined the US 'Pax Silica' strategic alliance in late 2025, fully aligning Dutch export policy with US interests. The regulatory trajectory is toward tighter restrictions, not relaxation. Further restrictions could expand beyond China or cover additional tool types, including older immersion DUV systems that remain exportable.

China imposed export controls on rare earth materials (holmium, thulium, ytterbium) used in EUV light sources. ASML has stated it holds stockpiles and is working on supply chain mitigation. Near-term impact is manageable but risk escalates if restrictions persist or expand.

macro.description: ASML is the central battleground in the US-China semiconductor technology conflict. Stock has historically sold off sharply on restriction announcements. The EUV component diversion allegation in June 2026 introduces a new and potentially severe vector. Further escalation — including FDPR application, full DUV bans, or military conflict scenarios — represents tail risk.

ASML's current growth thesis is predicated on AI infrastructure spending being durable. If AI monetization disappoints, hyperscaler capex could be cut abruptly, cascading through TSMC and Samsung capex reductions. ASML's order backlog provides 12-18 months of visibility but not multi-year protection against a true capex reversal.

ASML explicitly noted in its Q1 2026 forward-looking guidance that it 'accommodates potential outcomes of ongoing discussions around export controls' and tariff uncertainties. Broad US tariff expansion on European goods or semiconductor equipment could disrupt customer economics and ordering patterns.

execution.description: Successful High-NA EUV ramp is critical for ASML's 2026-2030 growth and margin expansion targets. High-NA has processed 500,000+ wafers at 80%+ availability as of Q1 2026, which is ahead of Low-NA at a comparable stage. However, full high-volume manufacturing qualification by Intel, TSMC, and Samsung still has execution risk.

Each EUV system requires ~100,000 components from 5,000+ suppliers. Ramping from 44 to 60+ Low-NA EUV units annually while simultaneously scaling High-NA production places material stress on the supply chain. Delays in component availability or sub-system qualification could limit shipment volumes.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Semiconductor equipment TAM expanding rapidly driven by AI infrastructure spending. ASML's addressable market for leading-edge logic and memory tools is growing as node transitions continue and the number of required EUV layers per chip increases. Long-term equipment demand underpinned by sovereign chip strategies (US CHIPS Act, EU Chips Act, Japan/Korea investment programs).
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - Revenue tied to semiconductor capex cycles, which historically swing 20-30% peak to trough. AI demand structural tailwind provides greater floor than prior cycles, but ASML is not immune to capital cycle dynamics. Q4 2025 record bookings of €13.2B (of which €7.4B EUV) suggest healthy near-term visibility.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect - Customer capex decisions are influenced by cost of capital. Elevated interest rates can delay fab investment decisions, though strategic imperatives around AI and geopolitical chip sovereignty mitigate rate sensitivity more than typical industrials.
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Moderate - ASML reports in euros but has significant USD-denominated revenue (US customers) and JPY, TWD, KRW exposures. A strong euro versus USD reduces the euro value of USD-priced system revenues. FX impact is a recurring guidance consideration.
key_input_costs: Rare earth materials subject to Chinese export controls (holmium, thulium, ytterbium)
Advanced engineering talent (43,882 FTE payroll employees as of Q1 2026)
R&D investment (~€4.7B in FY2025, critical to maintaining technology lead)

recent_developments.event: US EUV diversion allegation: Commerce Secretary Lutnick accused ASML in private meetings of allowing EUV machine components to reach China in violation of export controls. ASML formally denied the claims, documenting all 314 EUV systems worldwide are accounted for with none in China. US declined to provide specific evidence, citing source sensitivity. BIS enforcement action has been flagged as a potential outcome.
recent_developments.impact: Introduced a new high-severity regulatory risk; created stock volatility; damaged relations with key US government stakeholders at a critical trade policy juncture

recent_developments.event: MATCH Act introduced in US Congress: Bipartisan legislation would ban DUV lithography exports to China and compel Dutch alignment with US export control standards under threat of FDPR sanctions. Cleared House Foreign Affairs Committee on April 22, 2026 in what lawmakers called the largest export control markup in congressional history.
recent_developments.impact: Threatens remaining DUV China revenue (~5% of total sales); if service restrictions also enacted, could impact IBM revenues from installed Chinese DUV systems

recent_developments.event: Q1 2026 earnings: Revenue of €8.8B (+13% YoY), gross margin 53.0%, net income €2.8B, EPS €7.15 (+19% YoY) — all above consensus. Full-year 2026 guidance raised to €36-40B from prior €34-39B. Net bookings of €5.5B including strong EUV component. Management cited AI-driven customer capex acceleration.
recent_developments.impact: Positive earnings beat reinforced bull thesis; guidance raise drove stock higher, offset by stock dip on China export control commentary

recent_developments.event: FY2025 full-year results and Q4 2025 record earnings: FY2025 revenue €32.7B (+15.6% YoY), gross margin 52.8%, net income €9.6B, EPS €24.73. Q4 2025 net bookings a record €13.2B (of which €7.4B EUV). China was 33% of FY2025 revenue but expected to fall to ~20% in 2026. New €12B share buyback program (2026-2028) announced.
recent_developments.impact: Record bookings validated strong demand pipeline; guidance for 2026 of €34-39B (subsequently raised) highlighted China headwind but underlying non-China demand strength

recent_developments.event: First commercial High-NA EUV shipment: ASML shipped the EXE:5200B production-grade High-NA EUV system. Intel installed the tool for its 14A node development, becoming the world's first customer operating production-grade High-NA. SK hynix also began qualification runs. High-NA has now processed over 500,000 wafers at 80%+ availability, ahead of Low-NA at comparable maturity stage.
recent_developments.impact: De-risked High-NA technology transition; supports ASP expansion as High-NA carries ~€380-400M price vs ~€200M for Low-NA EUV

recent_developments.event: Netherlands formally joined US 'Pax Silica' strategic alliance, fully aligning Dutch export policy with US semiconductor technology restrictions.
recent_developments.impact: Reduces Netherlands-specific policy risk and uncertainty, but confirms current China export control regime will be maintained and likely tightened

recent_developments.event: AI hyperscaler capex commitments: Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, and Alphabet together announced over $300B in AI infrastructure capex for 2025-2026. TSMC raised 2026 capex guidance, and ASML's order backlog reached €38.8B at year-end 2025.
recent_developments.impact: Provides multi-year demand visibility and validates ASML's long-term revenue growth trajectory through 2027 and beyond

items.notes: Gross margin guided at 51-52% for Q2; reflects continued strong EUV demand but margin modestly below Q1 due to product mix

Raised from €34-39B at Q4 2025 earnings in January 2026. Guidance 'accommodates potential outcomes of ongoing discussions around export controls.' Midpoint of ~€38B implies ~16% growth vs FY2025. China expected at ~20% of 2026 revenue, down from 33% in FY2025.
Unchanged from initial 2026 guidance. Reflects product mix shift (High-NA ramp costs) and China revenue normalization. Q1 2026 came in at 53.0%, top of range.

Long-term scenario range from 2024 Investor Day, reaffirmed in 2025/2026 filings. Represents 35-84% growth from FY2025 revenue of €32.7B. Depends on semiconductor market scenarios and lithography intensity.
400-800 bps expansion from FY2025 driven by High-NA mix shift, operational leverage, and Installed Base Management scale. Reaffirmed at Q4 2025 earnings.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Christophe Fouquet (Q1 2026): 'The semiconductor industry's growth outlook continues to solidify, driven by ongoing AI-related infrastructure investments. Both Memory and Logic customers are responding to unprecedented demand by increasing capital expenditures and accelerating capacity expansion.' Management raised full-year 2026 guidance citing 'stronger immersion demand and incremental EUV upside concentrated in non-China customers.' High-NA EUV described as having processed 500,000+ wafers at 80%+ availability, ahead of Low-NA at a comparable development stage, de-risking the technology transition. Management noted Q1 2026 guidance 'accommodates potential outcomes of ongoing discussions around export controls,' signaling China-related uncertainty is actively factored into the outlook. CFO cited IBM sales growth as an increasingly important margin and revenue visibility driver.

bull_case: Irreplaceable technological monopoly: 100% market share in EUV lithography with a 30+ year lead on all competitors, backed by $9B+ in cumulative R&D, unique supply chain control (Zeiss optics, Cymer lasers), and $38.8B order backlog providing unprecedented revenue visibility. No credible commercial EUV alternative exists within the decade.

AI semiconductor supercycle sustaining beyond near-term: TSMC, Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron are all accelerating capex to meet AI chip demand, with hyperscalers committing $300B+ in AI capex for 2025-2026. ASML is the sole critical bottleneck in advanced chip manufacturing, making it structurally indispensable to the AI buildout.

High-NA EUV inflection drives significant ASP and margin expansion: First commercial High-NA EXE:5200B systems now shipping at ~€380-400M per unit vs ~€200M for Low-NA. As High-NA becomes standard for sub-2nm nodes (TSMC A14 from 2028, Intel 14A, SK hynix HBM next-gen), revenue per chip capacity unit will compound materially, driving ASML to its 56-60% gross margin target by 2030.

Installed Base Management as a durable compounder: IBM grew 26% YoY to €8.2B in FY2025 and continues expanding as the installed EUV fleet grows. IBM is structurally recurring, higher-margin than systems, and largely insulated from order cycle volatility — providing earnings quality above headline revenue numbers.

China risk already partially priced, significant non-China demand offsetting: Guidance explicitly factors in export control scenarios. Taiwan, Korea, US, and European customers are growing fast enough to more than absorb the China decline from 33% to ~20% in 2026. Any geopolitical relaxation or MATCH Act failure would be pure upside. UBS and Morgan Stanley both carry price targets of approximately €1,400 with strong buy ratings; average analyst consensus is ~€1,574.
bear_case: EUV diversion allegation creates existential regulatory risk: The June 2026 US accusation that ASML allowed EUV components to reach China — if escalated to a BIS enforcement action or FDPR application — could restrict ASML's ability to sell to any global customer using US-origin technology (which includes all leading-edge fabs). Even if ultimately resolved in ASML's favor, the diplomatic damage and compliance costs could be severe.

MATCH Act could eliminate remaining China DUV business: Proposed US legislation to ban DUV sales and service to China cleared the House Foreign Affairs Committee in April 2026. If enacted, it would eliminate ~5% of total revenue in permitted DUV sales plus additional IBM revenue from Chinese installed-base servicing — cumulatively a material hit to earnings.

Gross margin expansion trajectory at risk from High-NA ramp costs: Q3 2025 gross margin dipped to 51.6% as High-NA early production costs weighed on mix. The path from ~52-53% today to 56-60% by 2030 depends on successful High-NA commercialization at scale, sustained High-NA ASPs, and learning curve improvements — all carrying execution risk. Customer resistance to €380-400M per unit pricing could compress realized ASPs.

Semiconductor capex cycle reversal risk post-2027: Current bookings and backlog provide strong visibility through 2026-2027, but AI capex sustainability beyond that depends on AI monetization translating into revenue for cloud providers. Any perceived slowdown in AI ROI could trigger sharp capex cuts cascading through TSMC and Samsung to ASML. Historical semiconductor downturns demonstrate ASML is not immune — 2023 saw a ~14% EUV revenue decline.

Customer concentration and industry consolidation: TSMC alone represents ~33% of ASML revenue. Intel Foundry's ongoing struggles and potential strategic restructuring could reduce the number of High-NA EUV customers, concentrating risk further. Any major TSMC capex cut or geopolitical event affecting Taiwan would be a direct existential shock to ASML's revenue base.
